title: [YouPass Collect] - Australian exports to 4 countries from 1996 to 2001
prompt: The graph below shows the percentage of Australian exports to 4 countries from 1996 to 2001. Summarize the information by selecting and reporting the main features and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The line graph illustrates how Australia exported its products to four countries, including Japan, the US, China, and India, between 1996 and 2001.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was an increase in the proportion of Australian exports to India and China, with the most dramatic rise being seen in the latter, making it the largest export destination for Australia by the end of the period. In contrast, exports to the US and Japan experienced a decrease over the given timeframe.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Looking at the chart in more detail, in 1996, among the four destinations, India and China were the smallest export partners for Australia, with negligible figures of about 1% and 2%, respectively. Thereafter, China's importance increased significantly over the period, as the percentage of exports to this country rose steadily to 5% by 1998, before surging more than fivefold to around 27% in the final year. Likewise, India maintained a marginal presence in Australia's export market, at just 1% for the first decade, after which its share slightly increased, reaching a peak of about 7% in 2000, before falling back to 5% a year later.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: With regard to the remaining countries, in the first year, Japan was the leading destination for Australian exported goods, with more than a quarter of total exports going there, twice the figure for the US, at 11%. In the following years, the figures for Japan fell to about 17%, and stayed unchanged in the two final years. Similarly, the share of Australian exports to the US underwent a downward fluctuation throughout the period, bottoming out at 5% in 2000 before a modest recovery to 7% by the end of the period.
